drafted_from: tool row in tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-writing/tool-rows.json and test/test_writing_fine_tune.py, run here Nov 21 2026
start_here: Say to your AI: "Build my texting training rows from my sent messages into /work/texting, holding out the threads my test cases come from, 6 lines of thread, 10% for validation." It writes a request file and runs build_writing_pairs.py on your computer.
instructions: 1. Pour the two example rows into your own settings list (see pour), or make list:settings from them, then put your own system words, frame, base model and numbers in the build, train and write objects.

2. Keep your sent messages as rows (list:my-sent-messages): each with the thread before it and a plain draft made the same way as the cases you will measure on, and name the threads those cases come from.

3. Build the rows with tool:build-writing-pairs-from-a-persons-messages, train with tool:train-a-small-model-on-a-persons-writing (tens of minutes on a Mac with Apple silicon), then write the measuring cases with tool:write-with-a-persons-writing-adapter, once with the adapter and once with adapter null.
4. Compare both answers with your real messages on the same cases and keep the result rows; keep the adapter only where it beats the base model and your current way of writing.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a channel or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For the writing fine-tune the row id is record:setting:fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-writing~<scope_kind>~<scope_id> and its settings hold a build, a train and a write object that fill every request key the request leaves out.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read its fields and row type from your own store. Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the example rows to keep beside your own.
